title: Strange Wills
paragraphs: A syndicated anthology narrated by Warren William in which unusual wills, inheritances, and final wishes trigger stories of greed, revenge, romance, crime, and consequences after death.

Syndicated half-hour anthology built around unusual wills and inheritances. GRH contains 27 regular U.S. transfers representing 26 underlying program identities, plus one audition/sales presentation and six OTRR reference tracks. Market/distribution dates and numbering traditions conflict, so no single air-date or episode-number system is treated as universal.
GRH documents the program through U.S. Teleways/Charles Michelson transcription run (1946 to 1947).

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Albert Ulrich (director on 27 recordings), Del Castillo (organist on 27 recordings), Ken Krippene (writer on 27 recordings), Robert Webster Light (producer on 27 recordings), Warren William (performer on 26 recordings and host on 1 recording), Howard Culver (performer on 23 recordings), and [[person|lurene-tuttle|Lurene Tuttle]] (performer on 19 recordings).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include wills, estates and inheritance, probate law and heirs, romance and secret love, wealth, treasure and bequests, revenge from beyond the grave, and uncanny, supernatural or speculative motifs.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Postwar transcription syndication and local commercial insertion, Probate law as anthology framing device, and Australian continuation/repackaging after the U.S. package.
